correctness.rationale: The agent-level rate-one voter first-moment equation is ẋq=−D^(-1)Lq with root fixed, where L is positive definite grounded combinatorial Laplacian and D is the nonroot full-degree matrix. Integration from all-negative initial state gives La=d, hence cumulative dissent 1^T L^(-1)d, equal to the sum of fixed-root mean hitting times. A nonroot edge adds bb^T to L and e_u+e_v to d; substituting Sherman–Morrison yields the stated rank-one response with denominator 1+b^TPb>1. Independent Fraction Gaussian elimination across ALL connected labeled graphs and roots n=2,3,4 checked respectively 0,3,168 missing-nonroot-edge insertions, all 171 nonvacuous deltas strictly positive (minimum 2). For the five-vertex tree 01,04,12,23, hitting-time vectors before (5,8,9,1), after adding 24 (4,6,7,4), sums 23 and 21. Root-attached leaves each contribute exactly one independent unit of expected dissent in both graphs, extending the witness to all n>=5. The 16-state voter-chain certificate independently corroborates n=5.
residual_risks: Observable is cumulative person-time, explicitly NOT consensus time; graph clock and root assumptions are necessary.

value.rationale: Cumulative negative-opinion person-time is a natural, explicitly normalized transient cost under an immutable source. The result identifies the smallest network size where adding an ordinary peer link can SPEED conversion, despite universal worsening in all smaller networks, with an all-graph rank-one response to test interventions. The first failure at five and extension to arbitrary orders are mathematically motivated structural features, not merely an inverse-matrix exercise.
residual_risks: No sign classification for every larger graph or multiple zealots asserted.
